01Shuruaat — Interview Guide

Software Engineer Interview — Poora Overview

Sach ye hai ki top tech companies me job paane ke liye sauon LeetCode questions ghisne ki jaroorat nahi hai. Handbook ke mutaabik, sahi tareeke se taiyaari karo to kam questions me bhi offer mil sakta hai — handbook ke author ne 11 companies me interview dekar 9 offers haasil kiye the (Bay Area ki top tech companies — Facebook, Google, Airbnb, Palantir, Dropbox, Lyft aur kuch startups se). Ye guide technical aur non-technical — dono rounds ki taiyaari ka quick overview deta hai, aur har step ki detail ke liye handbook ke andar ke pages link kiye gaye hain.

Poori taiyaari 8 steps me banti hai. Pehle shortlist hone ke chances badhao, phir interview format pata karo, ek programming language chuno, Computer Science fundamentals taaza karo, coding interview ki practice karo, mid/senior level ke liye system design taiyaar karo, behavioral interview ki taiyaari karo, aur ant me offer package negotiate karo.

8 steps — ek nazar me

  1. Shortlist hone ke chances badhao — resume hi sabse important entry point hai. Bahut se qualified candidates sirf kharab resume ki wajah se shortlist nahi hote, qualification ki kami ki wajah se nahi.
  2. Interview format pata karo — quiz, online coding assessment, take-home assignment, phone screen, onsite — har company ka format alag hota hai.
  3. Programming language chuno — jo language sabse comfortable ho, wahi use karo. Python, Java, C++ aur JavaScript sabse common hain.
  4. CS fundamentals taaza karo — data structures aur algorithms ki neev pakki karo.
  5. Coding interview ki practice karo — structured plan se, andha-dhundh LeetCode ghisna nahi.
  6. System design taiyaar karo — mid/senior level ke liye zaroori hai.
  7. Behavioral interview ki taiyaari karo — har top company me kam se kam ek behavioral round hota hai.
  8. Offer negotiate karo — pehla offer kabhi best offer nahi hota.

Resume kyun sabse important hai

Shortlist hone ke baad aapke past achievements ka mahatva kam ho jaata hai — uske baad coding interview skills matter karte hain, jo method se seekhe ja sakte hain. Lekin screening stage tak pahunchne ke liye achievements ko sahi tareeke se frame karna padta hai. Resume likhne ka step-by-step guide isi handbook me hai.

Kaunse resources sabse useful hain

Handbook ke mutaabik practice ke liye ye resources sabse zyada kaam ke hain: Grokking the Coding Interview (patterns wala course), AlgoMonster (patterns + practice), aur handbook ke apne free guides — coding interview best practices, coding interview techniques, aur algorithms study cheatsheets. Paid courses lena zaroori nahi hai; free guides se bhi poori taiyaari ho sakti hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Interview ek skill hai — practice se behtar hoti hai. Mock interviews (interviewing.io jaise platforms par) se real interview ka pressure pehle se feel kar lo, taaki asli interview me ghabrahat na ho.
Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/software-engineering-interview-guide.md

02Shuruaat — Interview Guide

Coding Interview Ki Taiyaari — Step by Step

Coding interview ek technical interview hota hai jisme candidate ko programming problems dekar uski competency check ki jaati hai. Focus data structures aur algorithms par hota hai. Ek coding round aam taur par 30–45 minute ka hota hai — interviewer ek question deta hai aur candidate ko real-time collaborative editor (CoderPad/CodePen) ya whiteboard par code likhkar solve karna hota hai.

Evaluation ke 4 criteria

Top tech companies ke evaluation criteria lagbhag ek jaise hote hain, chahe naam alag hon:

  1. Communication — clarifying questions poochhna, approach aur tradeoffs saaf-saaf samjhana, taaki interviewer ko follow karne me dikkat na ho.
  2. Problem solving — problem ko samajhna, systematic approach, multiple approaches aur tradeoffs discuss karna, time/space complexity sahi nikaalna aur optimize karna.
  3. Technical competency — discussed solution ko working code me badalna, bina badi struggle ke. Clean, correct code, language ki achhi pakad.
  4. Testing — normal aur corner cases par code test karna, khud bugs dhoondhna aur sudhaarna.

Taiyaari ka sahi tareeka — 7 steps

  1. Ek achhi programming language chuno — jo familiar ho aur interview ke liye suitable ho (Python, C++, Java, JavaScript recommended).
  2. Time plan karo, topics priority order me karo — kitna time bacha hai, us hisaab se plan banao. Bare minimum ke liye lagbhag 30 ghante, achhi taiyaari ke liye lagbhag 100 ghante lagte hain.
  3. Ek topic padho, turant usi ki practice karo — memory retention ke liye study aur practice ek saath karo, alag-alag nahi.
  4. Cheatsheets ke saath practice karo — techniques, best practices aur algorithms cheatsheets ko practice ke dauraan saath rakho, taaki sahi aadatein shuru se banen.
  5. Self introduction aur final questions taiyaar karo — ye har interview ke start aur end me chahiye hote hain.
  6. Mock coding interviews do — interviewer ke saamne code likhne ka pressure pehli baar asli interview me feel na ho.
  7. Extra time ho to question patterns internalize karo — bahut se solutions me ek hi set of patterns repeat hote hain.
Galat tareeka: Seedha LeetCode kholkar hazaaron questions karna. 30 minute per question aur din ke 3 ghante practice se bhi 3–4 hafton me sirf lagbhag 160 questions honge — aur sahi approach internalize nahi hoga. Structured plan hi kaam karta hai.

Practice ke liye platforms: LeetCode (interview prep ke liye sabse suitable), HackerRank aur CodeForces (zyada competitive programming ki taraf). Grind 75 tool se apne bache hue time ke hisaab se custom study plan banaya ja sakta hai.

Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/coding-interview-prep.md

03Shuruaat — Interview Guide

3-Month Study Plan — Hafta-dar-hafta

Coding interview ki taiyaari ke liye recommended time 3 mahine (hafte me 11 ghante, matlab din me 2–3 ghante) hai — holistic taiyaari ke liye. Kam time ho to Grind 75 tool se apne time ke hisaab se plan generate kar lo. Core data structures aur algorithms se unfamiliar ho to pehle unhe revise karo, phir questions ki practice shuru karo.

Taiyaari ke 3 approaches

  • Breadth-first — pehle saare topics revise karo, phir saare topics ke mixed questions practice karo. Lagbhag 1 mahina ho to ye best hai.
  • Depth-first — ek topic ko poora master karo, phir agla topic. Time kam ho to High priority topics par focus karo.
  • Depth-first-then-breadth — ek-ek topic master karte jao, ant me mixed practice. 1 mahine se zyada time ho to ye best hai.

Handbook ki personal recommendation: Breadth-first ya Depth-first-then-breadth — taaki pehle wale topics bhool na jao. Time estimate hamesha conservative rakho, burnout se bacho.

Week 5–12: In-depth practice (75 questions)

Week 5 se 12 tak 75 questions ki list hai — Grind 75 tool se generate ki gayi. Week 1–4 me kuch questions pehle se kar chuke hoge, unhe skip kar sakte ho ya dobaara kar sakte ho. Dynamic programming questions skip kar sakte ho agar DP padha nahi hai — bahut se DP questions recursion/backtracking se bhi solve ho jaate hain.

Practice ke dauraan coding interview best practices aur techniques ko apply karna mat bhoolo — sirf questions solve karna kaafi nahi, sahi behavior bhi internalize karna hai.

Self introduction, final questions aur mocks ke liye time

Self introduction banane aur final questions taiyaar karne ke liye lagbhag 3 ghante rakho. Mock coding interviews tab schedule karo jab study plan ka 60% poora ho gaya ho — interview slots pehle se dikhte hain, advance me book kar lo.

04Shuruaat — Interview Guide

Top Companies Ke Interview Formats (9 Companies)

Har top company ka interview format alag hota hai. Neeche 9 companies ke formats hain — ye handbook me diye gaye hain aur time ke saath badal sakte hain, isliye apne recruiter se latest format zaroor confirm karo. COVID ke baad bahut si companies onsite rounds bhi remote karti hain.

Airbnb

Recruiter phone screen → 1–2 technical phone interviews (Algorithm/front end, CoderPad/CodePen). Onsite (General): 2 algorithm coding, 1 system design/architecture, 1 past experience/project, 2 cross-functional. Onsite (Front End): 2 front end coding (CodePen, koi bhi framework), 1 general coding apne laptop par, 1 past experience, 2 cross-functional. Tips: saare sessions apne laptop par coding — dev environment pehle se taiyaar rakho; APIs dekhne ki permission hai; compilable, runnable code par bahut zor hai; cross-functional interviews me cultural fit bahut important hai.

Asana

Recruiter phone screen → technical phone interview → onsite (Product Engineer): 3 algorithm + system design whiteboard ek hi session me, aur 1 session laptop par — 45 minute me 3 well-defined algorithm problems, phir engineer code review karega (code run nahi karna). Tips: front end questions nahi poochhe jaate; system design par bahut zor, whiteboard heavy; chaaron sessions me algorithms aur system design; ek session Engineering Manager leta hai.

Dropbox

Recruiter phone screen → 2 technical phone interviews (Algorithm/front end, CoderPad/CodePen). Onsite (Front End): 2 front end CodePen par (sirf Vanilla JS ya jQuery), 1 general coding CoderPad par, 1 all-round — Engineering Manager ke saath past experience aur working style. Tips: apne laptop par code kar sakte ho, APIs dekh sakte ho; ek front end session me Dropbox website ke ek real page ka pixel-perfect version banana hota hai, spec dekar.

Google

Recruiter phone screen → 1–2 algorithm technical phone interviews (Google Doc par). Onsite: 1–2 front end whiteboard par (Vanilla JS, kabhi-kabhi jQuery — Front End only), 2–4 algorithm whiteboard par, 1 General Cognitive Ability, Leadership aur "Googleyness" round. Phir team matching — alag-alag teams ke managers se baat. Tips: kabhi-kabhi phone interview skip karke seedha onsite bhi bula lete hain; non-fresh grads ko offer tabhi milta hai jab kisi team se match ho jaaye.

Indeed

Recruiter phone screen → technical phone interview (optional) → onsite: 1 online assessment HackerRank par (L0–L2), 1 resume discussion, 1–2 algorithm HackerRank par, 1 code review GitHub par, 1–2 system design (L3+), 1 technical presentation (L4+). Tips: role ke hisaab se bar alag hota hai; hiring decision aur leveling alag discussions hain; achha karo aur position bhar jaaye to doosre hiring managers packet utha sakte hain.

Lyft

Recruiter phone screen → 1 algorithm/front end technical phone interview (JSFiddle). Onsite (Front End): 4 front end CoderPad/apne laptop par (koi bhi language/framework), 1 behavioral — Engineering Manager ke saath resume par. Tips: whiteboard aur/ya laptop use kar sakte ho; front end coding ke liye React chuna ja sakta hai, project on-the-spot create-react-app se setup karna pad sakta hai.

Meta (Facebook)

Recruiter phone screen → 1–2 algorithm/front end technical phone interviews (Skype/CoderPad). Onsite: 2 technical coding whiteboard par, 1 behavioral (Engineering Manager, past experience/working style), 1 design/architecture whiteboard par. University Grad onsite: 2 technical coding, 1 behavioral. Tips: sirf whiteboard (ya wall) — laptop nahi; behavioral round ke ant me ek chhota technical question bhi aa sakta hai (front end candidates ko chhota HTML/CSS problem); coding rounds me speed ke hisaab se ek se zyada questions bhi mil sakte hain.

Palantir

Recruiter phone screen → 1 algorithm technical phone interview (HackerRank CodePair + Skype). Onsite (General): 2 algorithm whiteboard par, 1 decomposition (system design) whiteboard par. Onsite (Front End): 1 front end apne laptop par (lagbhag 1.5 ghante, koi bhi library/framework), 1 decomposition whiteboard par. Tips: React chuna ja sakta hai, project on-the-spot setup karna pad sakta hai; technical sessions ke baad Engineering Managers se milna achha ya bura sign nahi hai.

WhatsApp

Recruiter phone screen → 2 algorithm technical phone interviews (CoderPad). Onsite (Web Client Developer): 4 algorithm whiteboard par. Tips: front end questions nahi poochhe jaate; ek interviewer Engineering Manager hota hai.

Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/interview-formats-top-companies.md

05Shuruaat — Interview Guide

Mock Interviews — Asli Interview Se Pehle Practice

Interviewing ek skill hai — baar-baar rehearse karne se internalize hoti hai, tabhi steps second nature ban jaate hain. Practice ka achha tareeka hai kisi dost ke saath partner banna — ek-doosre ki baari-baari interview lo.

interviewing.io

Mock coding interviews ke liye sabse achha resource interviewing.io hai. Ye Google aur Facebook ke engineers ke saath anonymous practice technical interviews deta hai — anonymous hone se process de-biased aur low-risk rehta hai. Interview ke ant me interviewer aur interviewee ek-doosre ko feedback de sakte hain.

Mock interviews me achha karne par "jobs page" unlock hota hai — wahan se Uber, Lyft, Quora, Asana jaise top companies ke saath seedha (bhi anonymous) interviews book kar sakte ho. Mobile, Front End, Engineering Management jaise specific roles ke liye bhi mock interviews book kar sakte ho. Bilkul naye log recorded interviews dekhkar samajh sakte hain ki phone interview kaisa hota hai.

Kab mock interviews shuru karo

Mock coding interviews tab schedule karo jab study plan ka lagbhag 60% poora ho gaya ho. Interview slots interviewers dete hain, advance me dikhte hain — pehle se book kar lo. Behavioral mocks ke liye bhi interviewing.io par top companies ke professional interviewers milte hain.

Tip: Mock interview me bhi waise hi behave karo jaise asli me karoge — self introduction, clarifying questions, approach discuss karna, test cases — sab kuch. Tabhi sahi aadatein banengi.
Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/mock-interviews.md

06Shuruaat — Interview Guide

Career Landscape — Internship, Company Size, Geography

Is section ka zyada content Bay Area (US) ke liye likha gaya hai; geography ke differences neeche diye gaye hain.

Software Engineer ke roop me career prospects

  • High demand — lagbhag har domain technology use karta hai, isliye engineers har industry me chahiye. Demand supply se zyada hai, isliye salary aam taur par high hoti hai aur demand badhti ja rahi hai.
  • Stable career — Computer Science rapidly popular ho raha hai aur engineering ek highly-regarded professional career hai. Creative industry ki tarah top 1% hone ki jaroorat nahi — Silicon Valley me college se nikalte hi engineer ko USD 100,000 se zyada starting salary mil sakti hai.
  • Lifelong learning — technology industry bahut fast-moving hai. Aaj ki bahut si technologies ek decade pehle popular bhi nahi thi; 2009 me mobile app development aur blockchain lagbhag suna hi nahi gaya tha. Relevant rehne ke liye constantly upgrade karna padta hai.
  • Flexible — hours, location aur environment ke mamle me shayad sabse flexible job. Bahut si tech companies fully remote hain, formal attire nahi hai, working hours flexible hain.

Internships vs full-time

Top tech company me jaane ka sabse aasaan tareeka intern conversion hai. Internship interviews bahut chhote hote hain — aam taur par sirf 2 rounds, jabki full-time roles ke liye 4–5 rounds hote hain. Internship 3 mahine ki hoti hai, company aur engineering culture ko pehle haath samajhne ka mauka milta hai. High-performing interns ko return offers zyada milte hain kyunki wo prove kar chuke hote hain ki wo effective hain — hiring low-risk hoti hai.

Upar wala chart 2016 ke top US tech internships ki salaries dikhata hai — ye purana data hai, aaj ki salary isse bahut zyada hai. Sirf reference ke liye rakha gaya hai.

07System Design — Full Depth

System Design Interview Kya Hai — 4 Types

System design interview ka objective hai candidate ki skill check karna — real-world software systems design karne ki, jinme multiple components hote hain. Ye questions aam taur par zyada senior candidates (kuch saal ke experience wale) ko diye jaate hain. Interns ko system design questions aam taur par nahi diye jaate, kyunki unse relevant industry experience expect karna mushkil hota hai.

System design interviews ke 4 types

  1. Back end / distributed system design — multiple servers ya data centers par chalne wale systems design karne hote hain. Topics: back end architecture, database schema design, data replication, fault tolerance, message queues, consistency models, aur zyada.
  2. API system design — ek bade system ke andar APIs design karni hoti hain — HTTP APIs (jaise REST) ya software component ke andar methods.
  3. Object-oriented design — classes, objects aur unke relationships design karne hote hain. Class diagrams banana, interfaces define karna aur design patterns discuss karna padta hai.
  4. Front end system design — complex client applications ya UI components ki architecture design karni hoti hai. Client side par kya hota hai aur client-server ke beech API design par zyada focus hota hai.

Software engineers ko sabse zyada back end / distributed system design type milta hai. Isi liye is SPA me usi par sabse zyada depth hai.

Har design question ko approach karne ka framework

Handbook ki system-design.md khud ek resource list hai — usme step-by-step framework nahi diya gaya. Isliye neeche wala framework SPA me add kiya gaya hai, taaki har question ko end-to-end solve kar sako. Ye standard interview approach hai jo system design ki taiyaari ke liye use hota hai:

  1. Requirements clarify karo — functional requirements (system ko kya karna hai) aur non-functional requirements (scale, availability, latency, consistency) dono poochho. Scope agree karo.
  2. Capacity estimation (back-of-the-envelope) — users, requests per second, storage, bandwidth ka rough hisaab lagao.
  3. API design — main endpoints/methods define karo.
  4. Data model — kaunsi database (SQL vs NoSQL), tables/collections, indexes.
  5. High-level design — components ka diagram: client, load balancer, app servers, cache, database, message queue, storage.
  6. Deep dive — har component ki detail: scaling, replication, sharding, caching strategy, consistency.
  7. Bottlenecks aur tradeoffs — kahan fail ho sakta hai, kya tradeoff liya, aur aage kaise scale hoga.
Imandari se: Handbook ki system-design.md me 10 common questions aur resources ki list hai, framework nahi. Upar wala 7-step framework SPA ki taraf se add kiya gaya guidance hai — har question (sections 02–03) me isi framework se approach diya gaya hai.
Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/system-design.md

08System Design — Full Depth

10 Common Questions (1–5) — Approach ke Saath

Neeche handbook ke 10 sabse common back end system design questions hain. Har question ke saath framework-based approach diya gaya hai — kya clarify karna hai, kaunse components chahiye, aur kya tradeoffs discuss karne hain.

1. URL shortener design karo (jaise Bitly)

Clarify karo: kitne URLs per day, read vs write ratio, custom alias chahiye ya nahi, expiry chahiye ya nahi, analytics chahiye ya nahi. Estimation: 100M URLs/day ho to ~1160 writes/sec aur reads iske 100x tak ho sakte hain. Core idea: long URL → short code (Base62 encoding, 7 characters se 62^7 ≈ 3.5 trillion combinations). Components: API server, key-generation service (counter ya hash), database (key-value store), cache (hot URLs ke liye), redirect (301 vs 302). Tradeoffs: counter-based IDs predictable hote hain, hash-based me collision handle karna padta hai; read-heavy system hai isliye cache bahut important hai.

2. Social media website design karo (jaise Twitter)

Clarify karo: timeline, follow, tweet, like, search — kaunse features scope me hain. Core challenge: fan-out — ek celebrity ke tweet ko lakhon followers ki timeline me daalna. Do approaches: fan-out on write (tweet karte hi sab followers ki timeline me push — read fast, write heavy) vs fan-out on read (timeline kholte time pull — write light, read slow). Hybrid: normal users ke liye fan-out on write, celebrities ke liye fan-out on read. Components: user service, tweet service, timeline service, graph store (follow relationships), cache, message queue. Estimation: 300M DAU, har user din me 2–3 tweets — writes ~10K/sec, timeline reads ~200K/sec.

3. Video watching website design karo (jaise YouTube)

Clarify karo: upload, watch, search, recommendations, comments — scope kya hai. Core challenge: video storage aur delivery — videos bahut bade hote hain. Components: upload service, transcoding/encoding pipeline (ek video ko multiple resolutions me convert — 144p se 1080p), object storage, CDN (videos edge servers se serve hote hain), metadata database, search index, recommendation service. Key idea: video ko chunks me todkar stream karo (adaptive bitrate — network ke hisaab se quality badlo). Estimation: 500 ghante video har minute upload hota hai (scale ka andaza lagane ke liye) — storage petabytes me jaata hai, isliye CDN aur compression critical hain.

4. Chatting service design karo (jaise Telegram, Slack, Discord)

Clarify karo: 1-1 chat ya group chat, online presence, read receipts, media sharing, message history. Core challenge: real-time delivery — message bhejte hi doosre user tak pahunchna chahiye. Components: WebSocket/long-polling connection servers, message service, presence service (online/offline), message store (chat history ke liye), push notification service, media storage. Key ideas: har user ka persistent connection ek server se; message queue se fan-out; offline users ko push notification; message ordering ke liye per-chat sequence numbers; group chat me ek message ko saare members tak pahunchana. Tradeoffs: consistency vs availability — message deliver ho ya order sahi rahe, dono me balance.

5. File sharing service design karo (jaise Google Drive, Dropbox)

Clarify karo: upload/download, sharing, versioning, sync across devices, file size limits. Core challenge: bade files ko efficiently store aur sync karna. Components: block storage (file ko 4MB chunks me todna — sirf badle hue chunks upload hote hain, poori file nahi), metadata service, sync service, notification service, permission/sharing service. Key ideas: chunking + deduplication (ek hi chunk do users ke paas ho to ek baar store karo — hash se identify karo), delta sync, conflict resolution (do devices par ek hi file edit ho to version banao). Tradeoffs: strong consistency vs sync speed; storage cost vs deduplication ka CPU cost.

Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/system-design.md
← PehleSystem Design Interview Kya Hai — 4 TypesAgla →10 Common Questions (6–10) — Approach ke Saath
09System Design — Full Depth

10 Common Questions (6–10) — Approach ke Saath

6. Ride sharing service design karo (jaise Uber, Lyft)

Clarify karo: rider app, driver app, matching, pricing, trip tracking, payments. Core challenge: location-based matching real-time me. Components: location service (drivers ki live location — geohash ya quad-tree se nearby drivers dhoondho), matching service (nearest driver + ETA), trip service, pricing service (surge pricing), notification service, payment service. Key ideas: driver locations ko geospatial index me rakho; har kuch seconds me location update; rider request par nearby drivers me broadcast; accept karne par trip start; trip ke dauraan live tracking. Tradeoffs: exact nearest driver vs fast matching; surge pricing ka fairness.

7. Photo sharing service design karo (jaise Flickr, Pinterest)

Clarify karo: upload, feed, search, follow, likes/comments. Core challenge: images ka storage aur fast delivery. Components: upload service, image processing (thumbnails/resizing — alag-alag sizes generate karo), object storage, CDN, metadata database, feed service, search (tags/captions par). Key ideas: ek photo ke multiple sizes store karo (thumbnail, medium, original); feed ke liye fan-out on write; search ke liye inverted index. Tradeoffs: storage cost (multiple sizes) vs latency (on-the-fly resize slow hota hai).

8. E-commerce website design karo (jaise Amazon, eBay)

Clarify karo: product catalog, search, cart, checkout, payments, orders, inventory, recommendations. Core challenge: bahut saare microservices ka coordination aur inventory consistency. Components: catalog service, search service (Elasticsearch jaisa inverted index), cart service, order service, payment service, inventory service, recommendation service, notification service. Key ideas: inventory ke liye strong consistency zaroori hai (overselling nahi honi chahiye) — baaki cheezon me eventual consistency chalti hai; checkout ko saga pattern se manage karo (har step fail ho to compensate karo); flash sale/traffic spike ke liye queueing aur rate limiting. Tradeoffs: availability vs consistency — payment/inventory me consistency, recommendations me availability.

9. Jobs portal design karo (jaise LinkedIn, Indeed)

Clarify karo: job posting, search, apply, recruiter tools, recommendations, profiles. Core challenge: search aur matching — sahi jobs sahi candidates tak. Components: job service, search service (filters: location, salary, skills, experience), profile service, application tracking, recommendation service, notification service. Key ideas: jobs ko search index me daalo (inverted index on title/skills/location); matching ke liye skills overlap score; apply karne par application status workflow; recruiters ke liye candidate search (ulta direction). Tradeoffs: search freshness (nayi jobs turant dikhen) vs index update cost.

10. Web crawler design karo (jaise Google)

Clarify karo: kitne pages crawl karne hain, kitni baar refresh karna hai, robots.txt follow karna hai ya nahi. Core challenge: billions of pages ko efficiently aur politely crawl karna. Components: URL frontier (priority queue — kaunsa URL kab crawl karna hai), fetcher/downloader, parser (links nikaalna), dedup service (ek hi page dobaara crawl na ho — URL hash + content hash), storage (crawled pages), scheduler (popular pages zyada baar refresh). Key ideas: politeness — ek domain ko bahut zyada requests se hit mat karo (rate limit per host); duplicate detection ke liye Bloom filter ya hash set; crawl priority — PageRank jaisi popularity ya change frequency ke hisaab se. Estimation: 1 billion pages, har page 100KB ho to 100TB storage; 1000 pages/sec crawl karo to 1 billion pages me ~11 din lagte hain.

Yaad rakho: Interviewer ko perfect design nahi, sochne ka tareeka dekhna hota hai — requirements clarify karna, tradeoffs bolna, aur bottlenecks pehchanana hi asli signal hai.
Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/system-design.md

System Design — Quality Resources (Courses)

Handbook me system design ki taiyaari ke liye quality resources ki list di gayi hai. Neeche poori list hai — free aur paid dono alag sections me.

Courses aur guides

  • Front End System Design Playbook (GreatFrontEnd) — free guidebook, front end applications ke system design par focus. Facebook News Feed design, Google autocomplete search, Image Carousels jaise topics cover karta hai. Link: greatfrontend.com
  • System Design in a Hurry (HelloInterview) — ex-Meta aur ex-Amazon engineers dwara likha; basics, high-level concepts aur core technologies cover karta hai. Common problems ke worked examples hain, frequently updated, zyada content free aur high quality.
  • System Design Newsletter (SystemDesign.one) — weekly newsletter; free system design template bhi milta hai.
  • ByteByteGo — System Design Interview books ke author ka course. Basics ke baad 10+ famous products ke deep dives (YouTube design, Facebook Newsfeed, Chat System design) aur big data/storage systems. Har deep dive me concepts aur comprehensive diagrams hain, har seniority level ke liye approachable.
  • Grokking the System Design Interview (Design Gurus) — internet ka shayad sabse famous system design course. Purely text-based hai — reading prefer karne walon ke liye best. Popular system design problems ka repository + system design basics ka glossary hai.
  • Grokking the Advanced System Design Interview (Design Gurus) — same team ka advanced course; bahut senior ya specialist position ke liye hi zaroori hai.
  • System Design Interview Handbook (Educative) — complete interview-focused guide: scalable systems ko reason, communicate aur design karna, jaise top tech companies expect karti hain.
  • Grokking Modern System Design Interview (Educative) — ex-FAANG engineers ka structured course; bahut se system design topics + case studies.
  • Best of System Design package (Design Gurus) — dono Design Gurus courses ka bundle, discount par, lifetime access (subscription nahi).
  • System Design Interview Course (Exponent) — basics + popular system design questions ka bada database, mock interview videos ke saath. Kuch questions ke text answers, database schema aur APIs bhi hain. Subscription thoda pricey ho sakta hai, lekin Data Structures, Algorithms aur Behavioral Interviews ka content bhi milta hai — one-stop platform.
  • System Design Playlist (YouTube) — popular YouTuber ki playlist; har video ek alag system design topic cover karta hai, beginners ke liye simple tareeke se.
Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/system-design.md

13Coding Interview — Techniques & Cheatsheet

Solution Dhoondhne Ki 5 Techniques

Coding interview me sabse bada darr ye hota hai — agar question atak gaya aur solution nahi mila to kya hoga? Achhi khabar ye hai ki solution dhoondhne ke structured tareeke hain. Pehle clarifying questions poochho, phir kuch possible approaches interviewer ke saath discuss karo — wahin par zyada candidates atak jaate hain. Neeche ki 5 techniques se atakne se bacha ja sakta hai. Har technique har problem par apply nahi hoti, aur ek hi problem par multiple techniques bhi use kar sakte ho.

1. Problem ko draw karke visualize karo

Coding interviews traditionally whiteboard par isiliye hote hain kyunki diagrams se problem solving aasaan hota hai. Program ki internal state kaise badalti hai — ye diagrams se samajhna sabse aasaan hai. Agar solution samajh nahi aa raha, problem ka visual representation banao, aur jaroorat ho to har step par internal state banao. Ye technique khaas taur par useful hai jab input me trees, graphs, matrices ya linked lists hon. Example: matrix ke elements ko spiral order me return karna ho to matrix draw karo aur iterator ke har direction ke steps dekho — pattern khud dikhne lagega.

2. Problem ko haath se solve karo (bina code likhe)

Haath se solve karna matlab bina code likhe, jaise ek non-programmer karega. Ye aksar naturally ho hi jaata hai jab example samajh rahe hote ho. Kai baar working solution sirf manual approach ka code version hota hai — agar tum concrete rules bana lo jo har example par kaam karein, to code likhna aasaan ho jaata hai. Sabse efficient solution na bhi mile, shuruaat mil jaati hai aur credit milta hai. Example: binary search tree valid hai ya nahi — pehle check karo left subtree me sirf root se chhoti values hain, phir right subtree me sirf badi values, phir har node ke liye repeat karo. Ye process feasible lagta hai — ab ise code me badlo.

3. Aur examples banao

Chahe atke hue ho ya nahi, aur examples banana hamesha useful hai. Isse question ki samajh pakki hoti hai, jaldi code karne se bachte ho, pattern dikhta hai jo kisi bhi input par generalize hota hai — aur wahi solution hota hai. Plus, ye examples ant me test cases ke kaam aate hain jab solution verify karna ho.

4. Question ko chhote independent parts me todo

Agar problem bada hai, to high-level function se shuru karo aur use chhote functions me tod do, har ek ko alag solve karo. Isse details me doobte nahi aur soch structured rehti hai. Interviewer ko ye bhi dikhta hai ki approach hai, chahe saare chhote functions code na ho paayein. Example: Group Anagrams ko do parts me todo — string ko hash karna, aur strings ko group karna. Har part alag solve ho sakta hai. Dhyaan rakhna: sabse efficient solution ke liye kabhi-kabhi abstraction todkar ek hi pass me multiple operations karne padte hain — interviewer optimize karne ko kahe to wahi rasta hai.

5. Common data structures aur algorithms apply karo

Real-world software engineering se alag, coding interview problems chhote hote hain aur interview duration me solve hone layak design kiye jaate hain. Chahiye hua knowledge college me padhaya gaya hi hota hai. Common data structures ki list finite hai — ek hacky approach ye hai ki saare common data structures ko ek-ek karke problem par try karo. Frequency ke order me:

  • Hash Maps — lookup efficient banane ke liye. Interviews me sabse common data structure; use karna lagbhag pakka hai.
  • Graphs — data entities ke beech associations hon to graph model karke common graph algorithm use kar sakte ho.
  • Stack aur Queue — nested properties wali string parse karni ho (jaise mathematical equation) to stack hi chahiye hoga.
  • Heap — scheduling/ordering priority ke hisaab se ho, ya max K/min K/median elements nikaalne hon.
  • Tree/Trie — strings ko space-efficient store karna ho aur unki existence bahut fast check karni ho.

Routines: Sorting, Binary search (sorted input par O(n) se fast search), Sliding window, Two pointers, Union find, BFS/DFS, peeche se traverse karna, Topological Sorting.

Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/coding-interview-techniques.md

14Coding Interview — Techniques & Cheatsheet

Time Complexity Optimize Karna

Initial solution milne ke baad interviewer aam taur par poochhega — "Can we do better?" Neeche ki techniques time aur space complexity optimize karne me madad karti hain.

1. Best Theoretical Time Complexity (BTTC) pehchano

BTTC wo time complexity hai jise tum hara nahi sakte. Examples: array ke numbers ka sum nikaalna O(n) hai kyunki har value ko kam se kam ek baar dekhna hi padega. Group Anagrams ki BTTC O(nk) hai (n words, k max letters) kyunki har word aur har character ko kam se kam ek baar dekhna padega. Matrix me islands ginne ki BTTC O(nm) hai (n rows, m columns) kyunki har cell ko kam se kam ek baar dekhna padega.

BTTC jaanna isliye important hai taaki tum aisi solution dhoondhne ke chakkar me na pado jo BTTC se fast ho — fastest practical solution BTTC jitna fast ho sakta hai, usse fast nahi. BTTC hamesha practically achievable nahi hota, lekin usse fast koi real solution nahi ho sakta. Agar tumhara initial solution BTTC se slow hai, to improve karne ka scope hai. Interviewer ko BTTC batana positive signal hai.

Galatfehmi se bacho: BTTC hamesha total elements ke barabar nahi hota. Sorted array me number dhoondhna O(log n) hai (binary search), aur sabse bada number nikaalna O(1) hai (aakhri value). Isiliye question ki har detail par dhyaan do — galat BTTC nikaalna badi galti hai.

2. Overlapping aur repeated computation pehchano

Naive/brute force solution aksar wahi kaam baar-baar karta hai. Jab code mehenga operation dobaara kar raha ho, to socho ki pichhli computations ke results reuse kar sakte ho ya nahi. Dynamic programming (DP) iska sabse obvious example hai. Non-DP questions me bhi ye technique kaam aati hai, kabhi preprocessing step ke saath. Example: Product of Array Except Self — har index ke liye baaki sab values multiply karna O(n²) hoga. Lekin result[n] aur result[n+1] me bahut duplicated kaam hai — prefix array use karke O(n) time me solution mil jaata hai, thodi extra space ki keemat par.

3. Alag data structure try karo

Data structure ka choice coding interviews me sab kuch hai. Lookup slow hai to hash table se O(1) lookup karo. Example: K Closest Points to Origin — naive tareeka: distances nikaalo, sort karo, K smallest lo — O(n log n). Heap use karke O(n log k) ho jaata hai, kyunki heap ka size K par cap hai aur add/remove sirf O(log k) leta hai. Data structure badalne se efficiency me bahut farq pada.

4. Redundant kaam pehchano

Ye chhoti cheezein overall time complexity nahi badaltin, lekin coding ability evaluate hoti hai, isliye efficient code likhna important hai:

  • Bina jaroorat conditions check mat karo — if not arr and len(arr) == 0 me doosra check redundant hai; x < 5 and x < 10 me doosra check pehle ka subcondition hai.
  • Checks ka order dhyaan rakho — if slow() or fast() me fast() pehle rakho; if likely() and unlikely() me unlikely() pehle check karo taaki likely() run hi na ho.
  • Methods bina jaroorat invoke mat karo — array ki length baar-baar len(array) se mat nikaalo; shuru me length = len(array) variable bana lo.
  • Early termination — jawab milte hi return karo, poora loop mat chalao. Example: array me string hai ya nahi — milte hi return True karo.
  • Loop ke andar kaam minimize karo — search_term.lower() ko har iteration me call mat karo; loop se pehle ek baar lowercase karke variable me rakho.
  • Lazy raho — expression ko tabhi evaluate karo jab value chahiye ho. Strings khaali hon to search term lowercase karne ki bhi jaroorat nahi.
Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/coding-interview-techniques.md
← PehleSolution Dhoondhne Ki 5 TechniquesAgla →Space Complexity Optimize Karna
15Coding Interview — Techniques & Cheatsheet

Space Complexity Optimize Karna

Zyada tar time complexity space se important hoti hai. Lekin jab optimal time complexity mil jaaye, to interviewer space optimize karne ko keh sakta hai (agar solution extra space use kar raha ho).

1. Data ko in-place change karo / input overwrite karo

Agar solution intermediate processing/caching ke liye naye data structures bana raha hai, to memory allocate ho rahi hai — kabhi-kabhi ye negative mana jaata hai. Trick ye hai ki original input array ki values overwrite kar do, taaki nayi space allocate na ho. Lekin dhyaan rakho — input data ko irreversible tareeke se destroy mat karo, agar aage code me uski jaroorat ho.

Example: Dutch National Flag problem (Sort Colors) — O(n) time aur O(n) space me aasaan hai (naya array banao aur sort karke bharo). Lekin interviewer aam taur par O(n) time aur O(1) space maangta hai — input array ko in-place sort karo. Ek aur example: First Missing Positive — pehle loop ke baad saare values positive hain, to kisi number ki presence dikhane ke liye us index ki value negate kar do. Array ko hi hash table ki tarah use karo. Dhyaan rakhna: real software engineering me input mutate karna bura mana jaata hai — ye technique zyada tar coding interviews ke liye hai.

2. Data structure badlo

Phir se data structures! Kya tum best possible data structure use kar rahe ho? Example: strings ki list di gayi hai aur ginna hai kitni strings ek certain prefix se shuru hoti hain. Strings store karne ka efficient tareeka kya hai? Trie — tree jaisa data structure jo strings store karne me efficient hai aur prefix se shuru hone wali strings ginna fast kar deta hai.

Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/coding-interview-techniques.md
← PehleTime Complexity Optimize KarnaAgla →Interview Se Pehle Kya Karna Hai
16Coding Interview — Techniques & Cheatsheet

Interview Se Pehle Kya Karna Hai

Top candidates ke behavior aur evaluation criteria se best practices nikali gayi hain — interview se pehle, dauraan aur baad me kya karna hai, poora checklist. Ye guide practice shuru karne se pehle hi padh lo, taaki LeetCode practice ke saath sahi aadatein shuru se ban jayein.

General — interview se pehle

  • ✅ Comfortably dress karo — smart clothes ki jaroorat nahi, T-shirts aur jeans most jagah acceptable hain.
  • ✅ Self introduction aur final questions padhkar taiyaar rakho.

Virtual onsite coding interview se pehle

  • ✅ Pen aur paper taiyaar rakho — visualize karne ke liye; drawings trees/graphs questions me bahut helpful hain.
  • ✅ Earphones/headphones use karo, quiet environment me raho. Speakers use mat karo — echo se communication mushkil hota hai aur time waste hota hai.
  • ✅ Internet connection check karo.
  • ✅ Webcam aur audio check karo.
  • ✅ Coding environment (CoderPad/CodePen) ke shortcuts familiar karo aur setup karo — autocompletion, tab spacing, etc. Interviewers impress hote hain agar shortcuts aate hon.
  • ✅ Webcam band kar do agar possible ho — zyada tar remote interviews me video chat ki jaroorat nahi hoti, aur on rehne se distraction aur bandwidth waste hota hai.

Phone screen coding interview se pehle

  • ✅ Earphones use karo aur phone table par rakho — ek haath me phone pakadkar sirf ek haath se type karna mushkil hota hai.
  • ✅ Phone call ke bajay Zoom/Google Meet/Hangouts ya Skype ka option maango — links ya text bhejna aasaan hota hai.

Onsite whiteboarding interview se pehle

  • ✅ Whiteboard space management seekho — code lines ke beech jagah chhodo, taaki beech me lines insert kar sako.
Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/coding-interview-cheatsheet.md
← PehleSpace Complexity Optimize KarnaAgla →Interview Ke Dauraan Kya Karna Hai
17Coding Interview — Techniques & Cheatsheet

Interview Ke Dauraan Kya Karna Hai

1. Shuru me achha self introduction do

  • ✅ Ek-do minute me kuch sentences me introduce karo — self introduction guide follow karo.
  • ✅ Enthusiastic lago — smile ke saath bolo, engaging lagoge.
  • ❌ Self introduction par zyada time mat lagao — coding ke liye time kam ho jaayega.

2. Question milte hi clarifications karo

Turant code mat likhne lago. Coding questions jaan-boojhkar vague aur underspecified hote hain, taaki candidate ki attention to detail check ho. Kam se kam 2–3 clarifying questions poochho.

  • ✅ Question ko paraphrase karke interviewer ko wapas sunao — pakka karo ki exactly wahi samjha jo poochha gaya.
  • ✅ Assumptions clarify karo — tree jaisa diagram graph bhi ho sakta hai jisme cycles hon; naive recursive solution kaam nahi karega. Poochho: original array/graph modify kar sakte ho? Input kaise store hai? Words ki dictionary list hai ya Trie? Array sorted hai? (binary vs linear search decide hoga)
  • ✅ Input value range clarify karo — kitne bade inputs, kya range hai.
  • ✅ Input value format clarify karo — negative? floating points? empty? null? duplicates? bahut bade?
  • ✅ Ek simplified example se samajh check karo — palindrome checker ho to "KAYAK" → true, "MOUSE" → false jaise test cases banao aur interviewer se confirm karo.
  • ❌ Interviewer ki green light ke bina code mat likhne lago.

3. Interviewer ke saath approach work out karo aur optimize karo

Seedha code karna sabse buri galti hai — interviewers expect karte hain ki approach par 2-way discussion ho, time/space complexity analysis ke saath. Ye discussion kuch minute se 5–10 minute tak ho sakta hai. Is dauraan interviewer hints bhi de sakta hai.

  • ✅ Atak jao to structured techniques use karo.
  • ✅ Kuch approaches high level par explain karo (implementation detail me mat jao). Har approach ke tradeoffs discuss karo jaise interviewer tumhara coworker ho. Example: Two Sum — nested loops O(n²) time, O(1) space; ya ek pass me hash table O(n) time aur O(n) space. Dono discuss karo, tradeoffs batao, aur conclude karo kaunsi behtar hai (aam taur par kam time complexity wali).
  • ✅ Har approach ki time aur space complexity batao aur explain karo kyun (jaise nested loops ki wajah se O(n²)).
  • ✅ Best approach par agree karo aur optimize karo — repeated/duplicated/overlapping computations pehchano aur caching se kam karo.
  • ❌ Koi bhi di gayi information ignore mat karo. ❌ Apne approach ko lekar unsure mat dikho.

4. Solution code karte hue bolte raho

  • ✅ Code tabhi shuru karo jab approach explain kar di ho aur interviewer ne green light di ho.
  • ✅ Code karte hue explain karo kya achieve kar rahe ho — language mastery dikhao.
  • ✅ Reasonable speed se code karo — itna slow nahi ki time khatm ho jaaye, itna fast nahi ki explain na kar pao.
  • ✅ Actual compilable, working code likho, pseudocode nahi.
  • ✅ Clean, straightforward, neat code likho — kam se kam syntax errors/bugs. Complex messy implementation se clean simple implementation behtar hai.
  • ✅ Variable names aise rakho jo code explain karein — 3 ke multiples dhoondh rahe ho to results array ka naam multiplesOfThree rakho, array nahi.
  • ✅ Trivial functions use karne ki permission maango — reduce, filter, min, max use karna aam taur par OK hota hai.
  • ✅ Modular fashion me likho — high-level functions pehle, phir chhote helper functions. Agar trivial helper functions code na karne hon to interviewer se poochh lo.
  • ✅ Agar code me corners cut kar rahe ho to zor se batao aur kaho non-interview setting me kya karte — jaise "Non-interview setting me main regex likhta split() ke bajay."
  • ❌ Interviewer ko interrupt mat karo — aksar wo hints de rahe hote hain. ❌ Comments likhne me zyada time mat lagao. ❌ Khud ko repeat mat karo. ❌ Bure variable names use mat karo (bahut verbose ya single-character, i/n jaise common ones ke alawa). ❌ Code copy-paste karke check kiye bina mat chhodo.

5. Code karne ke baad check karo aur test cases add karo

Code khatm karke turant "done" announce mat karo. Interviewers expect karte hain ki tum mistakes scan karo aur test cases add karo.

  • ✅ Code ko mistakes ke liye scan karo — off-by-one errors jaise. Code ko aise padho jaise pehli baar kisi aur ka code dekh rahe ho, aur process bolte hue batao.
  • ✅ Interviewer ke saath edge cases brainstorm karo aur additional test cases add karo — bade inputs, empty sets, single item sets, negative numbers.
  • ✅ Un test cases se code ko step-by-step chalao.
  • ✅ Refactor karne ki jagah dekho.
  • ✅ Time aur space complexity dobaara batao.
  • ✅ Tradeoffs explain karo aur batao zyada time milta to kaise improve karte.
  • ❌ Turant "done" announce mat karo. ❌ Interviewer se argue mat karo — wo galat ho sakte hain lekin bahut unlikely hai, question unhe achhe se pata hota hai.

6. Interview ke ant me achhi impression chhodo

  • ✅ Company ke liye tailored achhe final questions poochho.
  • ✅ Interviewer ko thank karo.
  • ❌ Bina questions poochhe interview end mat karo.
Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/coding-interview-cheatsheet.md
← PehleInterview Se Pehle Kya Karna HaiAgla →Interview Ke Baad Kya Karna Hai
18Coding Interview — Techniques & Cheatsheet

Interview Ke Baad Kya Karna Hai

  • ✅ Interview questions aur answers note kar lo — future reference ke liye useful hote hain.
  • ✅ Interviewer(s) ko follow-up email bhejo ya LinkedIn invitation bhejo, time aur opportunity ke liye thank karo. Interviewer ke roop me ye lasting impression chhodta hai.
Yaad rakho: Interview ke baad ka follow-up chhota sa kaam hai, lekin bahut se candidates ise skip kar dete hain — yahi chhoti cheezein tumhe alag banati hain.

19Coding Interview — Techniques & Cheatsheet

Coding Interview Rubrics — Evaluation Kaise Hoti Hai

Kabhi socha hai Google, Amazon, Apple aur Netflix jaise top tech companies me coding interviews evaluate kaise hote hain? Terms alag ho sakte hain, lekin evaluated dimensions lagbhag same hote hain. Is guide me general evaluation process detail me hai, aur practice ke liye ek example rubric bhi hai.

Candidate scoring — 4 dimensions

  1. Communication — clarifications poochhna, approach communicate karna, code karte hue explain karna.
  2. Problem Solving — problem samajhna, sound approach, tradeoffs analysis, optimize karna.
  3. Technical Competency — implementation kitni fast aur accurate hai, syntax errors hain ya nahi.
  4. Testing — common aur corner cases par test karna, khud bugs correct karna.

Scoring ke 2 tareeke aur scoring bands

Do general methods hain: (1) har dimension ko score do (jaise 1–4) aur sum karo; (2) overall performance ke basis par ek overall score do. Scoring bands aam taur par: Strong hire, Hire, No hire, Strong no hire. Kuch companies me beech me ek band bhi hota hai jab interviewer ko aur assessment chahiye ho.

Score ka result par asar

Final score overall performance ke basis par hota hai, kisi mathematical cut-off se nahi. Phone screen me aam taur par 1 interviewer hota hai — "Leaning hire" ya usse upar na mile to aage nahi badhte. Clear signals na mile to follow-up phone screen bhi ho sakta hai. Zyada tar top companies full loop ke saare rounds karwati hain, phir final package par decision leti hain. Mixed results hon to interviewers discuss karte hain. Isiliye poori loop me performance important hai.

Additional assessment rounds tab bula sakte hain jab kuch aspects miss ho gaye hon (jaise 2 coding interviewers ne bahut similar questions poochhe hon), ya candidate ne kuch areas me mixed signals dikhaye hon. Scores aur feedback saare interviewers ko dikhte hain — kabhi-kabhi pichhli interviews ka feedback bhi dikhta hai, taaki wahi question dobaara na poochha jaaye. Companies dekhna chahti hain ki pichhli baar se growth hua hai ya nahi.

1. Communication — detail

Basic signals: appropriate clarifying questions, approach/rationale/tradeoffs communicate karna, code karte hue bhi constantly communicate karna, well-organized, succinct, clear communication.

ScoreOverall evaluation
Strong hirePoore interview me communication thorough, well-organized, succinct aur clear — question ki samajh, approach, tradeoffs sab. Interviewer ko candidate ki thought process follow karne me koi challenge nahi.
Leaning hireCommunication sufficient, clear aur organized. Lekin kuch aspects samajhne ke liye interviewer ko follow-up questions poochhne pade.
Leaning no hireCommunication insufficient (bina explain kiye code karne lage) ya disorganized/unclear. Interviewer ko thought process follow karne me difficulty hui.
Strong no hireKoi clarity se communicate nahi kar paaye ya address karne par bhi silent rahe. Interviewer ko extreme difficulty hui.

2. Problem solving — detail

Basic signals: achhe clarifying questions se problem jaldi samajhna, systematic aur logical approach, optimized solution, time/space complexity accurately determine karna, major hints ki jaroorat na padna. Advanced signals: multiple solutions, har solution ke tradeoffs saaf explain karna aur kaunsi current scenario ke liye best hai conclude karna, follow-up problems/extensions discuss karne ka time milna.

ScoreOverall evaluation
Strong hireSaare basic signals bina trouble ke, aur advanced signals bhi zyada tar achieve kar liye.
Leaning hireSaare basic signals achieve kiye, lekin advanced signals ke liye time nahi mila.
Leaning no hireSirf kuch basic signals dikhaye, baaki fail.
Strong no hireProblem solve nahi kar paaye, ya bina explanation ke kiya. Approach disorganized aur incorrect.

3. Technical competency — detail

Basic signals: discussed solution ko minimal/no bugs ke saath working code me badalna, clean straightforward implementation, no syntax errors aur unnecessary code, good practices (DRY, proper abstractions), neat coding style (indentation, spacing, variable naming). Advanced signals: multiple coding approaches compare karna, language constructs aur paradigms ki strong knowledge.

ScoreOverall evaluation
Strong hireBasic aur advanced signals effortlessly dikhaye.
Leaning hireSirf basic signals, approach ko code me badalne me kuch difficulty. Language paradigms ka suboptimal use.
Leaning no hireWorking solution produce karne me struggle. Multiple syntax errors, paradigms ka bura use.
Strong no hireWorking solution hi nahi bana paaye. Major syntax errors, paradigms ka bahut bura use.

4. Testing — detail

Signals: typical cases banana aur code ko un par test karna, corner cases dhoondhna aur handle karna, bugs identify aur self-correct karna, code ki correctness systematic tareeke se verify karna (debugger ki tarah har line step karna, har step par program state update karna).

ScoreOverall evaluation
Strong hireTesting signals effortlessly dikhaye.
Leaning hireTesting signals dikhane me kuch difficulty — saare relevant corner cases identify nahi kar paaye.
Leaning no hireTesting ki lekin corner cases handle nahi kiye. Bugs identify ya correct nahi kar paaye.
Strong no hireTypical cases par bhi test nahi kiya. Glaring bugs bhi nahi dekhe aur "done" announce kar diya.
Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/coding-interview-rubrics.md

Practicing hi coding interviews ki taiyaari ka best tareeka hai. LeetCode par hazaaron questions hain — kaunse practice karne hain? Blind 75 ke author ne sabse important 75 questions curate kiye the, phir unhe aur distill karke sirf 50 questions ka 5-week schedule banaya. Bahut se doosre LeetCode questions inhi questions ki techniques ka mash-up hote hain.

Practice karte waqt ise real coding interview ki tarah treat karo — submit karne se pehle thoroughly check karo, khud test cases banao aur unse verify karo. In questions ki LeetCode list bhi handbook me link ki gayi hai (Premium wale questions ke alawa).

21Practice Questions, Languages & Courses

Coding Interview Ke Liye Kaunsi Language Chunein

Kya coding interview me use ki jaane wali programming language matter karti hai? Jawab hai — haan. Zyada tar companies koi bhi language use karne deti hain — ek exception Google hai, jahan algorithmic coding interviews ke liye sirf Java, C++, JavaScript ya Python allowed hain. Lekin choice performance par bahut asar daal sakti hai, isiliye taiyaari ki shuruaat me hi sahi language chun lo aur practice me wahi use karo.

3 considerations

1. Suitability for interviews

Kuch languages interviews ke liye zyada suitable hoti hain — higher-level languages jaise Python ya Java me standard library functions aur data structures hote hain, jinse solution ko code me badalna aasaan hota hai. Interviewer ke roop me dekha gaya hai ki zyada tar candidates Python ya Java chunte hain; JavaScript, Ruby aur C++ bhi common hain. C ya Go jaise lower-level languages bilkul avoid karo — standard library functions/data structures kam hote hain aur manual memory management bhi karna pad sakta hai.

Python de facto choice hai kyunki succinct hai aur standard library me bahut functions/data structures hain. Python ke APIs different data structures par consistent hote hain — len(), for ... in ..., slicing notation. Aakhri element arr[-1], reverse arr[::-1] — minimal syntax me bahut kuch ho jaata hai. Java bhi decent choice hai, lekin types baar-baar declare karne se extra typing hoti hai — whiteboard par ye aur zyada dikhta hai. C++ ke reasons Java jaise hi hain. Ultimately Python, Java aur C++ decent choices hain.

CategoryLanguages
RecommendedPython, C++, Java, JavaScript
Acceptable (lekin recommended prefer karo agar familiar ho)Go, Ruby, PHP, C#, Swift, Kotlin
AvoidHaskell, Erlang, Perl, C, Matlab
You must be madBrainfuck, Assembly

2. Tumhari familiarity

Zyada tar cases me wahi language use karo jisme tum extremely familiar ho — sirf interview ke liye nayi language seekhna achha idea nahi hai. Language master karne me time lagta hai, aur agar zyada tar time algorithms par lag raha ho to language ke liye energy nahi bachti. Agar work me Java use kar rahe ho aur doosri language comfortably seekhne ka time nahi hai, to Java hi use karo — work vs interview me context switch se bacho. Zyada tar bottleneck sochne me hota hai, likhne me nahi.

Nayi language seekhne ke valid reasons: interview me us language ki jaroorat ho (mobile/front end/data science jaise domain-specific roles); tumhe interview shuru karne ki jaldi na ho. Poor reasons: company us language ko heavily use karti hai aur tum interviewer ko impress karna chahte ho; trendy dikhna chahte ho.

3. Exceptions

Domain-specific positions (Front End/iOS/Android) me us domain ki language chahiye hoti hai — JavaScript, Objective-C/Swift aur Java respectively. Agar language me koi data structure nahi hai (jaise JavaScript me Queue ya Heap), to interviewer se poochho ki kya tum assume kar sakte ho ki specified time complexities wala data structure available hai. Agar us data structure ki implementation solution ke liye crucial nahi hai, to interviewer aam taur par allow kar dega. Sahi data structures select karna, unki intricate implementation jaanne se zyada important hai.

Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/programming-languages-for-coding-interviews.md

23Practice Questions, Languages & Courses

Interviewer Cheatsheet — Do's aur Don'ts

Ye list technical interview ke interviewers ke liye hai — algorithmic interviews ke Do's aur Don'ts, straight-to-the-point. Candidates ke liye ye page crucial nahi hai, lekin interviewers kya dekhte hain ye samajhna helpful hota hai. Legend: ✅ = Do, ❌ = Don't, ⚠️ = Situational.

Before interview

  • ✅ Surroundings well-lit hon, quiet environment aur achha internet connection ho.
  • ✅ Webcam aur audio working hon; VC app test kar lo.
  • ✅ 2–3 questions taiyaar rakho aur unke alag-alag approaches se familiar raho. Achhe questions ke multiple solutions hote hain, har ek ke alag tradeoffs.
  • ✅ Knowledge gaps identify karne ke liye alag-alag topics se questions chuno.
  • ✅ Coding environment (CoderPad/CodePen) se familiar raho — shortcuts setup karo, autocompletion, tab spacing, etc.

Introduction

  • ✅ Poochho candidate ko restroom ya break chahiye ya nahi.
  • ✅ Interview format ka overview do (introduction, duration, available programming languages, ant me 5 min Q&A).
  • ✅ Khud ka introduction do aur candidate se introduce karwao.
  • ✅ Samjhao ki multiple questions honge, saare finish karna zaroori nahi hai, aur tum beech me abruptly interrupt kar sakte ho.
  • ❌ Candidate ko self introduction par zyada time mat lene do.

Question deliver karte waqt

  • ✅ Poochho candidate ne question pehle dekha hai ya nahi.
  • ✅ Question ke liye chhota example aur desired output do.
  • ✅ Candidate se pehle solution bolne ko kaho, coding me koodne se pehle.
  • ✅ Appropriate jagah hints do.
  • ✅ Hints ke baad bhi atak jaaye to solution dekar coding par chalo, taaki coding signals mil sakein.

Coding ke dauraan

  • ✅ Whiteboard interview ho to candidate ke saath khade raho, lekin space bhi do — door baithkar distant mat raho.
  • ✅ Saare positive aur negative signals note karo (rubric ke hisaab se).
  • ✅ Multiple questions hon to candidate ko ek question par zyada time mat lene do, khaas taur par agar pehla question Easy hai.
  • ❌ Time ko overly-obvious tareeke se check mat karo.

Coding ke baad

  • ✅ Candidate se test cases dene ko kaho aur code ko unke saath run karo.
  • ✅ Missed edge cases identify karo aur candidate se address karwao — seedha issue batane ke bajay poochho "What if X input hota? Tumhara code kya produce karta?"
  • ✅ Har question par kitna time laga, note karo aur feedback me likho.
  • ✅ Time complexity aur space analysis poochho.
  • ✅ Code preserve karo — photo lo ya code copy kar lo.
  • ✅ 5 minute bache hon to candidate ko roko ("I'll stop you here and let's go to the next section").

Wrap up aur post interview

  • ✅ Candidate ko questions poochhne do aur best effort se jawab do.
  • ✅ Candidate ko thank karo aur all the best kaho.
  • ✅ Feedback jaldi se jaldi likho, taaki bhool na jao.
Source:https://github.com/yangshun/tech-interview-handbook/blob/main/apps/website/contents/interviewer-cheatsheet.md
